name: The Shared-Owner One-Unit Holonomy Anomaly Is Impossible
statement: In the two-arm terminal setting with $|K|\le9$ and excess one, two two-concept cycle shores cannot meet in a common non-root owner. Hence the only one-unit profiles are an uncounted remainder of one with two disjoint two-concept shores, or disjoint cycle shores of orders two and three.
proof: Assume the shores are $\{r_1,o\}$ and $\{r_2,o\}$. Each root--owner pair is an active edge in a distinct direction. With zero uncounted remainder, each opposite collar is an ample three-vertex path and the punctured passive fiber over $o$ is forced. Since $|K|\le9$, the active lower slice has at most two vertices. Exhausting whether the collar roots coincide and which endpoint each collar meets shows that the one-inclusion graph of $K$ is a six- or eight-cycle with only tree edges attached and no square. If there are $t$ attached tree edges and the cycle has length $2m$, the isometric dimension is $m+t$, so only the empty set and $m+t$ singletons are strongly shattered. Thus $|\operatorname{SSh}(K)|=1+m+t<2m+t=|K|$, contradicting ampleness.
